data.name: Qiraatuh
data.gender_notes: Qiraatuh is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The phrase 'Qiraatuh' is derived from the Arabic words 'Qiraa' (to recite) and 'Tuh' (her). It refers to the recitation of the Quran by a woman. This name is often given to a girl who is believed to have a strong connection with the holy scripture. The name Qiraatuh carries the meaning “Recitation of the Quran” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Qiraatuh usually hope their child will grow to embody recitation of the quran and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Signifies a deep connection with the Quran and a strong commitment to the religious teachings.
data.etymology: Qiraatuh belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Recitation of the Quran.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Qiraatuh total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_arabic.name: قرأتُه
